subject: Clarification on data retention / deletion SLAs, backups & log windows — next steps
messages:

Thanks for the call this morning, Vivek. Quick recap and a few follow-ups we need before we proceed to legal/procurement: 

- SOC 2 status — can you confirm whether Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report and whether it covers the Hosted API? If the report is under NDA, please point me to the request process.
- GDPR / HIPAA applicability — we need to confirm the controls around PHI in the hosted flow and any contractual language you recommend for our DPA.
- Data deletion SLA — primary ask: when a customer requests deletion, what is the guaranteed SLA to remove data from service storage and any downstream logs?
- Backups & snapshots — do your backups contain customer content? If yes, how long are backups retained and what is the immutable window?
- Log retention — we need clarity on application logs vs. access logs vs. audit logs (retention windows, access controls, and export for eDiscovery).

I attached our retention questionnaire (Medix_Retention_Q_20261023.xlsx) — we filled the top-level items from the call but left the questions about backup retention and deletion from snapshots blank. Can your security team populate those?

Next steps I'd propose: you provide a short answer matrix for the items above, plus your SOC 2 summary. If all looks reasonable, we'll route to procurement for an initial purchasing LOI.

Thanks — Laura

Laura — thanks for the clear checklist and for the call this morning. Looping in Neha (security) and Monica (solutions) to fill the questionnaire and attach our SOC2 summary. High-level answers to unblock procurement: 

- SOC 2: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report that covers the Hosted API and the shared control plane. The full report is available under NDA; we can provide a redacted SOC2 summary (attached) immediately.
- GDPR/HIPAA: Hosted API can be used for PHI under our Business Associate Agreement (BAA). We offer contractual language in the DPA that restricts processing and details subprocessors.
- Deletion SLA: Primary production data is removed within 24 hours of an approved deletion request. Deletion from backups is handled according to the backup retention policy below (we provide a 30-day backup retention by default; see options).
- Backups & snapshots: Backups contain customer data for disaster recovery. Default retention is 30 days; snapshots are immutable for 7 days (cannot be altered), after which normal retention policies apply. Enterprise customers can request extended retention or shorter immutability windows via contract.
- Logs: Access logs and application logs are retained 90 days by default. Audit logs tied to compliance investigations can be retained longer on a case-by-case basis — we support export for eDiscovery and can provide S3-compatible exports on request.

Attaching a short SOC2 summary and a retention matrix draft. Neha — can you populate the attached Medix worksheet with the finer details (encryption, key management, RPO/RTO, deletion from immutable snapshots)?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Laura / team — I populated the Medix_Retention_Q_20261023.xlsx and exported our retention matrix (redwood-retention-matrix-v2.csv) attached. Key clarifications below — please quote these in your procurement/security review as needed.

1) Deletion flow and SLA
- Primary data deletion: once a deletion request is authenticated (via admin console + ticket), the data is queued and removed from active storage within 24 hours. We return a deletion confirmation ticket number.
- Backup deletion: backups are immutable for a short window (7 days) to support safe rollbacks. After immutability expires, snapshots are marked for deletion and purged according to the configured retention period. Default purge from backups is within 30 days of the deletion request; upon contract we can commit to a 14-day backup purge SLA for enterprise customers.

2) RPO / RTO and snapshots
- Default RPO: 24 hours for customer-configured state.
- RTO: Recovery time objective for Hosted API is SLA-backed per Dedicated customers; for Hosted we commit to operational runbooks and best-effort recoveries with status updates via the console.

3) Logs
- Access logs (who/when): retained 90 days by default.
- Audit logs (admin actions): retained 365 days for enterprise customers with increased retention as add-on.
- Export: Logs can be exported to a customer-owned S3 bucket on a daily cadence for eDiscovery; we provide a script and temporary credentials.

4) Encryption and keys
- All customer data and backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256. Customer-managed keys via KMS are supported for Private deployments and available as an add-on for Hosted.

5) PHI handling (HIPAA)
- We support a BAA and document controls around access, logging, and encryption. Processing of PHI is restricted to designated clusters when requested.

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf (SOC 2 executive summary), redwood-retention-matrix-v2.csv (detailed matrix). I also added answers inline in your spreadsheet.

If Medix needs a quicker backup purge SLA (e.g., <30 days), propose that in your reply and we can surface it to commercial/legal for a commitment.

-Neha

- Please confirm the process for issuing a SOC 2 NDA and a point of contact for compliance to sign the NDA.
- We'll need the export script + sample S3 policy so our infra team can validate automated daily exports.

Next steps for us: we'll queue this with procurement if you can confirm the 14-day backup purge and provide the NDA link + export artifacts. Looping Evelyn for onboarding scheduling after procurement confirms.
